abstract: This study investigates how seven right-leaning media organizations use cross-platformization strategies to reach audiences on both Twitter and Truth Social during the 2022 U.S. midterm election. Analyzing content volume and story packaging, the authors combine computational and qualitative methods to examine how outlets curate their posts differently across the two platforms. The findings indicate that outlets shared only a small share of their total stories across both platforms, suggesting platform-specific curation practices.
key_claims: Right-leaning media organizations employ distinct cross-platformization strategies when distributing content across Twitter and Truth Social.
Only a small portion of an outlet's total stories are posted across both platforms, indicating selective and platform-tailored curation.
Story packaging and content volume differ by platform, reflecting strategic adaptation to each platform's audience or environment.
methods: Collection of social media posts and content from seven right-leaning media organizations on Twitter and Truth Social.
Focus on the 2022 U.S. midterm election period as the case study.
A mixed-methods design combining computational analysis with qualitative analysis.
Analysis focused on two dimensions: content volume and story packaging.
findings: Outlets posted only a small share of their total stories across both Twitter and Truth Social.
Content curation and packaging varied between the two platforms (further findings not fully available from the abstract).
contributions: Introduces and applies the concept of cross-platformization to right-leaning media's social media practices.
Provides empirical insight into how partisan media curate content differently across mainstream (Twitter) and alternative (Truth Social) platforms.
Offers a mixed-methods framework for studying multi-platform media distribution during a major U.S. election.
framing: The paper situates itself within research on platformization, partisan media, and the alternative media ecosystem, examining how right-leaning outlets navigate both mainstream and alt-tech platforms. It contributes to political communication scholarship on cross-platform content strategies and media curation.
